subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add an agent-controlled pre-compaction lifecycle contract, and if so should bounded deferral be in scope now?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but handoff and deferral would add public config plus extra agent authority, workspace-write timing, checkpoint semantics, and possible approval carryover.

options.title: Adopt warning and checkpointed handoff first
options.body: Add opt-in threshold warnings plus a structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

options.title: Adopt full bounded deferral
options.body: Allow DEFER semantics only with explicit max duration, audit trail, idempotent checkpoint matching, workspace scope, and approval-expiry rules.

options.title: Decline new lifecycle surface
options.body: Keep memoryFlush, notifyUser, hooks, and checkpoint APIs as the supported compaction surfaces and document recovery patterns.

recommendation.title: Adopt warning and checkpointed handoff first
recommendation.body: Add opt-in threshold warnings plus a structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice extends the memoryFlush lifecycle that steipete introduced, with security-sensitive scope beyond a narrow code repair.
